papers.title_en: ReGATE: Recurrent Gated Visual Fusion for Reactive Humanoid-Object Interaction
papers.authors: Hao Zhu, Jorge Peña-Queralta
papers.evidence: 融合第一视角深度与本体感知的感知驱动人形全身控制器
papers.tldr: 人形机器人移动操作需在机载感知下完成抓取、搬运与释放，并应对指令和视觉不完整。ReGATE 以教师-学生框架融合第一视角深度、本体感知与在线运动/接触指令，用循环适配器估计交互状态，并以门控调节视觉更新。仿真中静态目标抓取成功率85.2%，高于VisualMimic的48.5%，移动目标达85.9%。该工作将循环门控视觉融合拓展到视觉中断下的人形移动操作。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinating object acquisition, transport, and release from onboard sensing while responding to user commands and incomplete visual observations. We present ReGATE, a whole-body controller that combines egocentric depth, proprioception, and online locomotion and contact commands. Built on a teacher-student framework, ReGATE integrates interaction-state estimation through a recurrent adapter that predicts object geometry and physical contact without an external object-pose estimator. Head-wise and global gates regulate visual updates to a proprioceptive pathway. A visual-grounding and corruption curriculum trains the adapter, while phase-aware initialization increases coverage of brief contact transitions. In simulation, ReGATE achieves 85.2% success across 330 static-object acquisition trials, compared with 48.5% for VisualMimic under the same protocol, and 85.9% across 440 moving-object acquisition trials. Deployment on a Unitree G1 demonstrates commanded grasp-transport-release sequences and acquisition of laterally displaced boxes. A qualitative hardware experiment further demonstrates successful box acquisition when the camera is occluded after an initial observation and before the contact command. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to extend recurrent gated fusion of onboard depth and proprioception from perceptive locomotion to humanoid loco-manipulation under interrupted visual sensing.

papers.title_en: STEP: Spatiotemporal Training with Explicit Prediction for Perceptive Humanoid Locomotion
papers.authors: Youhao Lyu, Chenghao Sun, Zhenxuan Ding, Shuting Zhang, Ziyang Dong, Wenhao Cui
papers.evidence: 具备显式时空预测的感知型人形机器人运动控制
papers.tldr: 针对感知式人形机器人行走中地形几何依赖身体状态与动作演化的问题，STEP提出单阶段时空训练框架，在共享控制表征中联合监督跨模态关系与动作相关状态演化。它用可学习查询聚合深度和本体感知token为紧凑策略状态，以双向掩码预测和动作条件预测器显式约束地形—身体关系及下一融合状态。仿真中地形通过性优于融合替代与消融，视觉退化下更鲁棒；23自由度Noetix E1实机100次试验成功98次，覆盖楼梯、40cm平台、70cm沟槽、踏石和无后向视觉后退楼梯。
papers.abstract_en: For perceptive humanoid locomotion, the relevance of terrain geometry depends on the robot's body state and how both evolve under its actions. Existing work has advanced terrain-aware sensory fusion and cross-modal prediction, improving how visual and proprioceptive information is combined and related. However, feature aggregation alone does not specify which cross-modal relationships should be learned, while prediction between simultaneous observations does not explicitly constrain their action-dependent evolution. We present Spatiotemporal Training with Explicit Prediction (STEP), a one-stage framework that jointly supervises cross-modal relationships and action-dependent state evolution within a shared control representation. Multiple learned queries aggregate depth and proprioceptive tokens into a compact policy state. Bidirectional masked prediction uses each visible modality to predict latent features of the omitted modality, explicitly supervising terrain-body relationships. An action-conditioned predictor maps the current policy state and executed action to the next fused state, with an exponential-moving-average target defined directly in the policy representation space. Simulation comparisons show overall improvements in terrain traversal over evaluated fusion alternatives and ablations, while depth-dropout and delay experiments demonstrate the benefits of both predictive objectives under degraded visual input. Deployed on a 23-DoF Noetix E1 humanoid with onboard sensing, STEP succeeds in 98 of 100 hardware trials across stairs, a 40\,cm platform, a 70\,cm gap, stepping stones, and backward stair traversal without rearward terrain visibility.

papers.title_en: LocoMuJoCo: A Comprehensive Imitation Learning Benchmark for Whole-Body Control
papers.authors: Firas Al-Hafez, Davide Tateo, Oleg Kaidanov, Aditya Bhatt, Artur Zelik, Zhengyi Luo, Jan Peters
papers.evidence: 含人形本体与仿真到真机部署的全身控制模仿学习基准
papers.tldr: 面向全身控制的模仿学习与强化学习缺少统一、可复现的评测平台。LocoMuJoCo 以单一 API 统一 MuJoCo CPU 与 MJX/MjWarp GPU 后端，提供 9 个人形、3 个（肌）骨骼和 4 个四足本体，并内置人形动作捕捉数据与 AMASS/LAFAN1 重定向。其插件化架构可替换观测、奖励、控制模式、地形与域随机化，配合紧凑 JAX 算法实现 JIT 端到端训练。该开源基准还提供 sim-to-real 部署仓库，降低全身控制算法比较与落地门槛。
papers.abstract_en: LocoMuJoCo is an open-source benchmark for imitation learning (IL) and reinforcement learning (RL) on whole-body control. The library couples MuJoCo (CPU) with MJX and the MjWarp backend (GPU) under a single API, exposes 9 humanoid, 3 (musculo-)skeletal, and 4 quadruped embodiments, and ships a curated native motion-capture dataset for every humanoid, to which it can also retarget AMASS and LAFAN1. A modular plug-in architecture makes observations, rewards, control modes, terrains, and domain randomization fully interchangeable, while compact JAX implementations of many RL and IL algorithms provide JIT-compiled end-to-end training, and the companion loco-mujoco-real repository provides sim-to-real deployment. We describe the design, the SMPL-to-robot and robot-to-robot retargeting pipeline, and a usage example. LocoMuJoCo is released under MIT at https://github.com/robfiras/loco-mujoco.

papers.title_en: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Sihang Li, Xiaofeng Guo, Jinkun Cao, Charlie Cheng, Ruihan Yang, Chen Feng, Guanya Shi, Haozhi Qi
papers.evidence: 结合扩散策略与全身控制器的力反应人形移动操作
papers.tldr: 日常接触任务不仅需要运动轨迹，还要求人形机器人协调双手与全身的接触力。FLORE 用两只带力感知的 UMI 手持夹爪和可穿戴追踪器采集无机器人演示，训练以视觉、本体感知和测得力旋量为输入的力反应扩散策略，输出动作与每手力指令。混合柔顺全身控制器结合力跟踪维持平衡，在仿真中准确跟踪不同方向与大小的手部力。真实机器人三项接触任务成功率达80%，显著高于仅位置策略的26.7%。
papers.abstract_en: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone. Therefore, we present FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation. We collect robot-free demonstrations using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers for hand motion and contact wrenches, and wearable trackers for body motion. A force-reactive diffusion policy takes vision, proprioception, and measured wrenches as input, then predicts actions and per-hand force commands. A hybrid compliance whole-body controller with force tracking executes these commands while maintaining balance: an integral of the force error measured by real force/torque (F/T) sensors lets each hand track force accurately along the commanded direction and remain compliant along the others. In simulation, the controller tracks per-hand force commands of varied magnitude and direction, with little loss in whole-body motion accuracy. Across three contact-rich tasks on the robot, the force-reactive policy succeeds in 80% of rollouts, compared with 26.7% for a position-only policy trained on the same demonstrations and executed by the same controller. For more details, please visit our website: https://louis-leee.github.io/FLoRe/.

papers.title_en: Whole-Body Humanoid Control via Stochastic Motion Tokenization
papers.authors: Michael Drolet, Oleg Arenz, Jan Peters
papers.evidence: 随机运动标记化为人形全身跟踪策略生成运动参考
papers.tldr: 人形机器人全身控制难以仅靠速度指令，且现有RL跟踪策略缺乏未来运动信息，不利于行为切换。作者提出随机运动tokenization，将运动压缩为可由行为标签或文本命令生成的离散token，并直接作为全身跟踪策略的参考。在Unitree G1上，该tokenizer重建精度优于FSQ和VQ-VAE；离散接口驱动真实机器人完成16.8秒舞蹈、格斗、行走及35秒格斗转舞蹈序列。结果表明简洁随机运动表示可作为高层控制与全身跟踪之间的有效接口。
papers.abstract_en: While velocity-commanded RL policies are effective for controlling quadrupeds, they are a limited interface for humanoids that need to perform complex whole-body motions. Furthermore, RL tracking policies for whole-body motions typically have limited information about the desired future motion, preventing them from performing controlled deviations to achieve long-term task success; such information is particularly relevant when a controller must prepare for transitions between behaviors. We address these challenges using concise motion representations that can be generated by a high-level controller, given a behavior label or text command. These representations can be fed directly into a tracking policy to provide a detailed motion reference. Our method exhibits a high degree of flexibility in performing real-world robot motions such as dancing, fighting, or walking based on conditional information. At matched capacity, our adopted stochastic motion tokenizer reconstructs motions from the Unitree G1 at a level that exceeds state-of-the-art approaches such as finite scalar quantization (FSQ) and the vector-quantized autoencoder (VQ-VAE). The resulting discrete interface conditions whole-body tracking policies that execute generated dance, fight, and walk motions lasting 16.8 s each and a 35 s fight-to-dance sequence on a physical Unitree G1.

papers.title_en: HC2Robot: Hyper-Connection Transformers with Predicted Foresight for Multi-Terrain Humanoid Parkour
papers.authors: Wenhao Xu, Yanheng Mai, Yifei Fu, Nan Zheng, Yanbo Zhou, Zirui Huang, Mingsheng Ling, Xinjue Wang, Renjing Xu
papers.evidence: 融合特权前瞻学习的感知型人形跑酷
papers.tldr: 人形机器人跑酷需在高度不连续地形上预判落脚点与全身动作，而可部署策略只能依赖机载感知。HC2Robot 通过预测前瞻模块 PFM 从可部署观测预测下一步触地时机、位置与支撑质量，并用 HC Transformer 的多流路由增强时序推理。在楼梯、沟壑、高台和斜坡上，仿真平均通行成功率达 97.60%，安全落脚率优于强基线。该工作将特权监督转化为可部署表征，缩小训练与部署的信息差。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid parkour requires robots to reason about future footholds and whole-body motions over highly discontinuous terrain. We revisit the information asymmetry in asymmetric actor-critic learning for perceptive humanoid locomotion: the critic exploits privileged simulator signals during training, whereas the deployable actor operates solely from onboard perception. We argue that the key is not exposing privileged information to the actor, but learning a deployable approximation of it to narrow the information gap between training and deployment. We present HC2Robot, a deployable perceptive humanoid parkour framework consisting of a Predicted Foresight Module (PFM) and a Hyper-Connection (HC) Transformer. PFM predicts from deployable observations the policy-conditioned timing, location, and support quality of each foot's next touchdown event, converting privileged supervision into a deployable latent representation that provides the actor with predicted touchdown information without privileged runtime sensing. The HC Transformer further enhances temporal reasoning through learnable multi-stream routing, while a future motion prediction head provides short-horizon motion priors for regularization. Across stairs, gaps, high platforms, and slopes, HC2Robot achieves a mean simulated traversal success rate of 97.60% and consistently higher safe foothold rates than strong perceptive locomotion baselines, supporting improved traversal performance and geometric foothold support under deployable sensing.

papers.title_en: FORGE: Feasible Online Reduced-Order Reference Generation and Whole-Body Execution for Agile Humanoid Locomotion
papers.authors: Adrian B. Ghansah, Yujin An, Jeeseop Kim, Soon-Jo Chung
papers.evidence: 降阶参考生成与全身跟踪结合的人形控制
papers.tldr: 针对人形机器人敏捷运动需在线生成可行参考并稳定全身跟踪的问题，FORGE提出两阶段学习框架：先以单刚体动力学结合全身运动学训练命令条件参考生成器，再冻结该降阶模型策略在线生成参考，训练全阶全身跟踪策略。在Unitree G1上实现纵向-2.0至2.8 m/s、横向±1.0 m/s、角速度±3.0 rad/s，并完成单腿跳跃与连续指令切换。该统一框架覆盖广指令空间和多运动策略，兼顾参考可行性与全身执行。
papers.abstract_en: This paper presents a two-stage learning framework for versatile and agile humanoid locomotion that couples online reduced-order model (ROM) reference generation with whole-body tracking control. In the first stage, we train a command-conditioned whole-body reference generator using single rigid body dynamics combined with full humanoid kinematics. In the second stage, the frozen ROM policy is rolled out online to generate references for training a whole-body tracking policy on the full-order dynamics model. Learning a kino-dynamically consistent reference generator in the simplified ROM space enables us to generate references over a broad command space and over multiple locomotion strategies using a single unified framework. We demonstrate the approach on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot, achieving longitudinal velocities from -2.0 m/s to 2.8 m/s, lateral velocities up to +-1.0 m/s, angular velocities up to +-3.0 rad/s, one-legged hopping, and continuous transitions across the commands, all using one unified reference policy and one whole-body tracking policy.

papers.title_en: METATRON: A Promptable Whole-Body Execution Layer for Humanoids
papers.authors: Chen Tessler, Yifeng Jiang, Alec Otto, Yi Shi, Umar Iqbal, Gal Chechik, Xue Bin Peng
papers.evidence: 面向人形的可提示全身执行层与生成式基础策略
papers.tldr: 人形控制器常需任务专用训练，难以复用平衡与全身协调能力。Metatron将生成式基础策略与可编程技能层结合，基础策略接收身体目标、速度与风格提示并生成多样全身动作，训练后冻结。技能以普通代码在每步构造提示，并由编码智能体分析运动数据拟合规则，无需再训练策略。在Unitree G1上单一检查点支持行走、恢复、遥操作拾取与坐家具，并提升到达成功率与抗推鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid controllers often require task-specific training despite sharing the need for balance and whole-body coordination. We present Metatron, a promptable whole-body execution layer combining a generative base policy with a programmable skill layer. The base policy receives partial goals, collectively called a prompt, that can combine timed body-part targets, velocity commands, and style cues. It produces diverse whole-body motions consistent with these goals. Training combines motion capture, synthetic recovery trajectories, and retargeted scene-interaction motions. After training, the policy is frozen. Stateful programs called skills express task intent as prompts at each control step, drawing rough geometric sketches that the policy turns into coordinated movement. Skills are ordinary code, refined by coding agents that analyze motion data and fit compact rules without task-specific policy training. On the physical Unitree G1, one frozen checkpoint supports walking, recovery, teleoperated object pickup, and sitting on furniture. Comparative evaluations show higher reaching success and push robustness than the tested reference-tracking pipelines. The same recipe produces climbing and acrobatics on a simulated character. Metatron enables coding agents to turn learned motor capabilities into new skills through code, without further policy training.

papers.title_en: HIPC: Humanoid Iterative Planning and Control via Goal-Conditioned Motion Closure
papers.authors: Yi Han, Xingyu Chen, Zixuan Lang, Qianyang Wu, Yuhang Lin, Ji Ma, Liang Li, Dongting Li, Xinpeng Liu, Ruoli Dai, Hesheng Wang, Renjing Xu, Lei Han
papers.evidence: 面向全身运动的人形迭代规划与控制
papers.tldr: 现有生成式人形全身运动方法多采用开环“生成器+控制器”，跟踪误差会累积成空间漂移，且规划器难以根据真实执行反馈应对扰动；直接闭环又因真实状态偏离训练分布引发抖动甚至跌倒。HIPC 将生成式运动规划与跟踪控制耦合为实时迭代规划控制框架，用规范运动表示实现目标条件规划，并以偏差衰减恢复和历史重锚定缓解分布偏移，配合异步规划控制与延迟补偿。实验表明其在多条件切换与组合下取得领先目标到达精度，并能抵抗物理扰动、从跌倒中恢复。
papers.abstract_en: Recent generative models are widely used to provide whole-body motion for humanoid tracking. Current methods combine motion generators with controllers in an open-loop paradigm, which leads to critical issues: tracking errors can accumulate into spatial drift, and the planner cannot adapt to unexpected physical disturbances without feedback from physical execution. However, directly feeding realized states back to the planner in a closed loop can cause discontinuities, resulting in physical jitter and even falls, since such states are out of distribution during training. To bridge this gap, we propose HIPC, a real-time Humanoid Iterative Planning and Control framework that couples a generative model with motion tracking into a unified planning-and-control paradigm. HIPC introduces a goal-conditioned motion planning trained with a canonical motion representation that avoids gimbal-lock singularities under extreme orientations and supports motion generation on diverse geometric and semantic conditions. Then, HIPC adopts two strategies, deviation-decayed recovery and history re-anchoring, to mitigate the out-of-distribution shift caused by realized-state feedback. Finally, HIPC operates a real-time asynchronous planning-and-control system, with latency compensation to reduce temporal mismatch for inference delay. Extensive experiments confirm the effectiveness of HIPC under switching and composition of diverse conditions. Results show that HIPC achieves state-of-the-art goal-reaching accuracy among existing methods while simultaneously demonstrating robustness to physical perturbations and the ability to recover from falls.

papers.title_en: OneSteer: Unlocking Steerable General Humanoid Motion Tracking via One-Step Diffusion Whole-Body Control
papers.authors: Yifei Huang, Yazhao Yang, Li Weijia, Tianle Shi, Ji Jin, Zhihui Cai, Zihao Liu, Jianzhuang Zhao, Songlin Dong, Xinyuan Chang, Yihong Gong, Dian Shen, Zhiheng Ma
papers.evidence: 单步扩散全身控制实现人形运动跟踪
papers.tldr: 人形机器人部署常只给目标结果，却仍需遵循部分原始参考，通用跟踪与测试时转向难兼顾。OneSteer以一步扩散全身控制器统一二者：冻结权重，用可微任务代价优化输入噪声，并以身体分组掩码放松指定跟踪约束。仿真中1.25米横杆净通过率从2%升至90%；Unitree G1完成27次名义跟踪不摔倒，仅靠机载LiDAR通过1.1米低杆并跨12厘米障碍。预测状态-动作计划作为共享接口，支持反馈执行与失败预判，并可指导定向微调。
papers.abstract_en: Deployment objectives often specify desired outcomes without providing revised trajectories, while parts of the original reference must still be followed. We present OneSteer, a one-step diffusion whole-body controller that combines general motion tracking with selective test-time steering. To accommodate new objectives, differentiable task costs guide optimization of the generator's input noise with frozen weights, while body-group reference masks relax selected tracking requirements. Predicted state-action plans provide a shared interface for task optimization and feedback-conditioned execution. For nominal tracking, the model trained from scratch achieves the lowest local tracking error among the evaluated baselines on successful held-out AMASS and BONES clips. For steering, one frozen distilled controller adapts across diverse deployment objectives in simulation, raising the clean passage rate under a 1.25 m bar from 2% to 90%. On a physical Unitree G1, OneSteer completes all 27 nominal tracking trials across nine diverse whole-body motion sequences without falling. With a steering cost derived from a signed distance field built using only onboard LiDAR, it also passes under a 1.1 m low bar in four of five attempts and steps over a 12 cm hurdle without falling in all three attempts. Beyond control, prediction variation in the model trained from scratch ranks likely tracking failures without physics rollouts. This scoring method is more than 10x faster than simulation-based scoring with five rollouts per clip and guides targeted fine-tuning. Project page: https://onesteer.github.io

papers.title_en: Anchor 1: Precise and Stable Humanoid Control for Whole-Body Manipulation
papers.authors: Archon Robotics, :, Caojun Wang, Checheng Yu, Gangcheng Jiang, Guangjun Zeng, Haoran Jiang, Hongyang Li, Huibin Yan, Huijie Wang, Jialong Zeng, Jin Yang, Kai Cheng, Li Chen, Liang Chen, Lirui Zhao, Modi Shi, Penglin Fu, Shijia Peng, Tianyu Li, Wencong Zhang, Xuechong Lv, Yixuan Pan, Yong Zhang, Yu Qiao, Yu Zhang, Ziyan Li
papers.evidence: 面向精确稳定全身操作的人形全身控制器及协调性基准
papers.tldr: 人形机器人全身操作对执行偏差敏感，微小误差或多余步态就可能导致任务失败。Anchor 1采用校准稀疏运动参考，避免在线关节空间重定向，并以离线筛选的机器人动作塑造训练分布，同时引入与运动编码解耦的显式误差反馈。仿真和硬件评测显示，在更严格真实评分下，跟踪误差较现有控制器降低30%至80%，且所需前瞻输入更少。该工作为精确稳定的全身操作提供了实用控制基础与系统基准。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid controllers have acquired increasingly diverse motor skills, yet translating these capabilities into precise and stable whole-body manipulation remains challenging. Manipulation tasks are sensitive to execution deviations -- even small errors or unintended steps can cause failure. Introducing Anchor 1, a whole-body controller for precise and stable whole-body manipulation, together with a benchmark spanning diverse coordination demands. Anchor 1 adopts calibrated sparse motion references to preserve task-relevant human motion structure without online joint-space retargeting, leaving kinematic freedom for precise control. To guide this freedom towards stable, physically plausible whole-body coordination, we shape the training distribution through offline curation of robot motions paired with these calibrated sparse references. We further introduce explicit error feedback decoupled from motion encoding, improving control precision while supporting flexible command interfaces. To achieve a systematic evaluation of these capabilities, a benchmark is proposed to assess precision, sustained execution stability, and reachability across diverse whole-body coordination demands. Evaluations in simulation and on hardware show stronger precision and stability across all evaluation tracks. Under the most strict real-world global scoring setting, Anchor 1 achieves a 30\% to 80\% decrease in tracking error with fewer look-ahead inputs, and without retargeting compared to all existing controllers. Downstream experiments demonstrate more efficient teleoperated data collection and higher task success using the same deployment pipeline as well. We believe Anchor 1 supports precise and stable whole-body control as a practical basis for humanoid task execution.

papers.title_en: Learning Agile Humanoid Dodgeball with Onboard Monocular Vision
papers.authors: Feng Tian, Yulin An, Chenhao Li, Matthias Heyrman, Marco Hutter
papers.evidence: 机载单目感知与学习式全身闪避恢复控制相结合
papers.tldr: 人形机器人在共享动态环境中需在保持平衡的同时躲避高速来物。作者构建了集成机载单目视觉、时序球状态与威胁标志估计、学习式全身控制的躲避球系统，并组合躲避/恢复与搜索/跟踪策略、采用三阶段课程训练。仿真中5米、6米/秒来球成功率97.8%–100%，2.5米、10米/秒降至33.2%–40.8%；Unitree G1实机单次躲避成功率超85%。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid robots operating in shared, dynamic environments must respond to rapidly approaching objects while maintaining balance. We study dodgeball as a controlled test of this capability, coupling visual threat assessment with whole-body evasion, recovery, and target reacquisition. We develop a system that integrates onboard monocular perception, temporal ball-state and threat-flag estimation, and learned whole-body control. A ball detector supplies bounding-box histories, and a temporal estimator predicts relative ball position and a binary threat flag. Separate dodge/recovery and search/track policies share this interface and are composed to support repeated encounters. A three-stage curriculum first trains control with privileged ball states, then starts estimator supervision from stable policy rollouts, and finally replaces the actor's privileged inputs with estimator outputs. Analytic projection and perception randomization provide detector-like training observations without image rendering. Across approach-angle bins in controlled simulation, dodge success ranges from 97.8--100.0% for 5.0 m launches at 6 m/s to 33.2--40.8% for 2.5 m launches at 10 m/s, with 1000 throws per speed--distance condition. On a physical Unitree G1, controlled single-throw success exceeds 85% over more than 15 trials. A hardware sequence demonstrates full-azimuth target reacquisition followed by another dodge. These results demonstrate an integrated onboard-monocular-vision system under highly dynamic motions.

papers.title_en: HuG: Learning Humanoid Whole-Body Affordance-Aware Grasping with Active Perception
papers.authors: Xuanbin Peng, Lai Wei, Yuze Zhai, Qingyuan Yu, Keyi Wang, Jianglong Ye, Xiaolong Wang
papers.evidence: 结合主动感知与全身运动的人形全身可供性抓取
papers.tldr: 人形机器人在第一视角遮挡下取物困难，需全身协调并保持基座稳定。HuG以“感知-对齐-抓取”流程耦合主动感知与全身可供性策略，将视角作为决策变量消解遮挡，并用点云条件策略生成抓取。训练引入控制器闭环动力学筛选，剔除73%运动学可行但不稳定的抓取。仅仿真训练即在多层货架取得87.5%真实成功率，各高度至少73%，展现空间外推能力。
papers.abstract_en: Acquiring objects in human environments is hard for humanoids: targets are partially occluded under egocentric viewpoints, and reaching them demands coordinated whole-body motion that keeps the target visible and reachable while the base stays stable. We present HuG, a framework for whole-body affordance-aware grasping with active perception that couples perception and action through a Perceive-Align-Grasp pipeline: belief-driven active perception resolves occlusion by treating viewpoint as an explicit decision variable; a point-cloud-conditioned affordance policy proposes whole-body grasps; and an affordance-aware alignment stage repositions the body to the most executable configuration. A key insight is that, on a floating base, kinematic validity is not enough: we curate training data with controller-in-the-loop dynamics simulation, rejecting 73% of kinematically valid grasps that would destabilize the deployment controller, so the policy learns kinodynamically feasible affordances. Trained entirely in simulation with zero real demonstrations, HuG attains 87.5% real-world success on a multi-level shelf task, generalizes to novel objects, and holds at least 73% success at every tested height. Beyond generalizing within its training distribution, the policy extrapolates spatially: at scale in simulation it succeeds at table heights well below any seen during training, indicating that kinodynamically filtered synthetic data grounds affordances in object geometry and whole-body feasibility rather than in memorized configurations.

papers.title_en: CompliantBot: Learning Whole-Body Compliance across Task Interfaces for Humanoid Control
papers.authors: Haoyang Li, Keqi Zhu, Zhanxiang Cao, Yang Zhang, Yizhi Chen, Xuekang Yang, Yue Gao
papers.evidence: 面向人形控制的全身柔顺性训练框架
papers.tldr: 人形控制器需在外力下屈服并随后恢复任务，但跟踪目标与合规偏差存在冲突，现有方法依赖特定接口或构造数据，难以跨任务复用。CompliantBot用状态依赖交互力场耦合负载与运动，并以力幅奖励和任务奖励动态加权协调屈服与恢复，无需外力测量或合规数据。在运动跟踪与速度指令两类接口上，它屈服更远、弹簧负载更低，撤力后恢复跟踪，强拉力下任务完成最高且关节机械功率最低。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid controllers need the ability to yield to external forces while retaining the capacity to resume their original tasks. However, tracking objectives penalize the deviations needed for yielding, while relaxing tracking goals persistently can make task recovery harder. Existing approaches often rely on task-specific interaction command interfaces or constructed compliant motion data and reference trajectories, limiting the direct reuse of their compliance-training mechanisms across different task interfaces. We introduce CompliantBot, a compliance-training framework for motion tracking and velocity-command locomotion. It preserves the original task inputs and requires no preconstructed compliant data or target trajectories. A state-dependent interaction force field couples applied loads to the robot's motion, enabling local articulation and whole-body movement to change the forces experienced. A complementary force-magnitude reward encourages lower interaction loads, while task rewards are downweighted during loading and restored after release to coordinate yielding and task resumption. The trained policies use task inputs and proprioceptive history without explicit external-force measurements. Across both task interfaces, CompliantBot yields farther under constant pulls and experiences lower spring interaction loads than matched baselines, while resuming task tracking after force removal. CompliantBot achieves the highest task completion among the compared methods under stronger pulls. Power evaluations further show that CompliantBot has the lowest mean joint mechanical power among the compared methods. Real-robot demonstrations further illustrate compliant responses through arm motion, stepping, and body reorientation.

papers.title_en: Online iLQR-MPC with Whole-Body Control for Robust Humanoid Locomotion
papers.authors: Xiang Li, Linlin Ou, Ruihan Wu, Xinyi Yu
papers.evidence: 在线 iLQR-MPC 结合全身控制实现鲁棒人形行走
papers.tldr: 人形机器人行走需同时决定落脚点与接触力，扰动会破坏标称规划，且约束随每次触地切换。该方法采用单刚体模型保留姿态动力学与完整接触力旋量，并用iLQR-MPC在单一滚动时域内联合优化接触力和落脚点，无需独立步态规划器。约束通过增广拉格朗日与松弛障碍罚项进入反向传播，全身控制器以500 Hz将规划映射为关节力矩。MuJoCo中重规划达100 Hz、平均求解8.9 ms，Unitree G1可稳定行走并从245 N前向和175 N侧向冲击中恢复。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid locomotion requires deciding where to step and how to distribute contact forces. However, a disturbance can invalidate the nominal plan, requiring coordinated revision under constraints that switch with every footfall. To solve this online, the proposed approach employs the single-rigid-body model, which retains attitude dynamics and the full contact wrench. An iterative linear-quadratic-regulator MPC (iLQR-MPC) then jointly optimizes contact forces and footstep locations in a single receding-horizon problem, without a separate step planner. Specifically, contact and motion constraints are incorporated into the backward pass through augmented-Lagrangian and relaxed-barrier penalties. A whole-body controller subsequently maps the plan to joint torques at 500 Hz while preserving contact feasibility. The model-based formulation makes disturbance responses interpretable through explicit costs and constraints, and requires no platform-specific policy training. In MuJoCo simulations, the iLQR-MPC replans at 100 Hz (mean solve time 8.9 ms); the Unitree G1 sustains steady-state walking and recovers from impulsive 245 N forward and 175 N lateral pushes.

papers.title_en: Contact-Implicit Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization for Dynamic Humanoid Locomotion on Parameterizable Uneven Terrain
papers.authors: Roberto Mauceri, Stefano Dafarra, Giulio Romualdi, Marco Gabiccini, Daniele Pucci
papers.evidence: 面向人形运动的接触隐式全身轨迹优化
papers.tldr: 人形机器人在复杂非平整地形上动态行走时，通常需要预先指定接触序列，限制了规划灵活性。本文提出接触隐式全身轨迹优化框架，用光滑曲面模型近似台阶、斜坡等可参数化地形，并设计新的接触约束把刚体交互从平面推广到任意光滑曲面。基于非线性规划生成无需预设接触序列的可行动态轨迹，在仿真与ErgoCub真机上完成非共面地形初步验证。
papers.abstract_en: This letter presents a trajectory planner for humanoid robots to perform dynamic motions on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. The planner generates feasible movements without predefined contact sequences, considering the robot's full dynamics and kinematics. To plan bipedal locomotion on steps, ramps, and other terrains, we propose a mathematical model to approximate ground geometry with a smooth surface. The rigid interaction between the robot and the ground is modeled via novel contact constraints, extending the domain of applicability from flat and horizontal surfaces to any arbitrary smooth surface. Effectiveness is demonstrated using nonlinear programming to plan motions on various terrain topologies. We also explore dynamic trajectory generation by embedding high-level requirements in the cost function and the initial guess. Preliminary feasibility tests were conducted over non-coplanar terrains, both in simulation and on the real robot ErgoCub.

papers.title_en: H^2MARL: Hierarchical Heterogeneous Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Humanoid Robot Control
papers.authors: Xuemin Hu, Kaixin Li, Qingqing Xia, Yuxin Wang, Wei Xie, Bo Tang, Long Chen
papers.evidence: 面向人形全身控制的关节自由度级分层异构多智能体强化学习
papers.tldr: 人形机器人全身控制面临高维耦合动力学与关节自由度物理异质性，现有MARL划分粗糙且层级规划与执行常分离。本文提出H^2MARL，按JDoF级物理异质性感知分解策略，并通过闭环策略-执行器联合优化共享交互轨迹，协调高层姿态规划与低层关节执行。MuJoCo与Isaac Gym实验显示，其在运动稳定性、步态协调和动作质量上持续优于同质、粗粒度及独立优化基线。该工作将异质多智能体建模与层级闭环协同统一于人形机器人全身控制框架。
papers.abstract_en: Coordinated whole-body control of humanoid robots remains challenging due to high-dimensional coupled dynamics and substantial physical heterogeneity across joint degrees of freedom (JDoFs). Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning methods either employ coarse agent partitions or directly apply generic heterogeneous-agent algorithms, while hierarchical controllers commonly optimize high-level planning and low-level execution independently, leading to uncoordinated motion. In this paper, we propose H^2MARL, a hierarchical heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement learning framework with two key mechanisms. We first formulate humanoid whole-body control using a JDoF-level physical-heterogeneity-aware policy factorization, where each torque-actuated JDoF is conditioned on an explicit descriptor of its actuation, kinematic, and dynamic properties. Moreover, we develop a closed-loop policy-executor co-optimization mechanism that jointly adapts the high-level pose planner and the low-level joint executor using shared interaction trajectories, thereby reducing the distribution mismatch between planning and execution. Extensive experiments in MuJoCo and Isaac Gym demonstrate that H^2MARL consistently improves locomotion stability, gait coordination, and motion quality over homogeneous, coarse-grained, and independently optimized alternatives.

papers.title_en: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
papers.authors: Siyuan Hu, Abulikemu Abuduweili, Yue Meng, Shipeng Liu, Quentin Leboutet, Chen Chen, Matthias Müller, Vladlen Koltun
papers.evidence: 在仿真中合成视觉-语言-运动数据，实现感知驱动的人形运动与导航
papers.tldr: 人形机器人要实现通用自主，受限于视觉-语言-动作配对数据的瓶颈：用遥操作采集一小时数据要消耗一小时人力。HALO 在程序化生成的千余个虚拟家庭中合成视觉-语言-运动数据，使语料规模随算力而非人力扩展。系统习得坐椅、导航到指定物体、侧身穿半开门、蹲爬钻桌、推箱等技能，并能组合这些技能完成长程任务；训练中从未见过真实家庭，却零样本迁移到现实，在六个未建图环境中完成360次试验，成功率达91%。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid robots have the potential to automate a wide range of physical tasks. Progress toward generalist humanoid autonomy, however, remains constrained by a data bottleneck: mapping pixels and free-form language to low-level joint commands requires paired supervision, and no corpus of such data exists at sufficiently large scale. Some approaches rely on human teleoperation and wearable capture devices, which require at least an hour of human time to produce an hour of data. We present HALO, a humanoid autonomy system powered by a pipeline that synthesizes vision-language-motion data across a thousand procedurally generated homes. The corpus scales with compute rather than human labor. HALO acquires a repertoire of physical skills, including sitting on chairs, navigating to named objects, stepping sideways through half-open doors, crouching and crawling beneath tables, and pushing boxes. It orchestrates these skills to solve composite, long-horizon tasks. Without ever seeing a real home during training, HALO transfers zero-shot to the physical world, achieving a 91% success rate across 360 trials in six unmapped real-world environments. See https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-halo/ for code and videos.

papers.title_en: CRISP: Constraint-Resolved Interactions between Subsystems for Predictive Whole-Body Cooperation
papers.authors: Dario Valenzuela, Jeeseop Kim
papers.evidence: 面向人形机器人的分层全身控制与约束解耦子系统交互
papers.tldr: 人形机器人全身协作面临高维动力学、双臂闭链约束与下肢支撑的耦合难题。CRISP将躯干、双臂和下肢分解为动态互联子系统，用完整约束和Lagrange乘子刻画肩部与末端交互力，并由高层NMPC联合优化子系统轨迹、臂力矩、地面反力和交互力。仿真与G1实验表明交互力与接触测量一致，双臂轨迹跟踪和全身协调稳定，NMPC可在线运行。该框架实现了约束解析的预测性全身协作，为高维人形动态操作提供可验证的分层控制途径。
papers.abstract_en: This paper presents a layered control framework that recasts high-dimensional system dynamics as a composition of dynamically interconnected subsystems, with dynamic dual-arm manipulation on the humanoid serving as a representative application. The humanoid is decomposed into a single rigid body (SRB) representing the torso and floating-base dynamic models representing the articulated arms and lower-body. The rigid connections between arm and torso and the closed kinematic chain formed between the end-effectors during cooperative manipulation are represented as holonomic constraints. The corresponding Lagrange multipliers parametrize the interaction wrenches transmitted at the shoulders and between the end-effectors. The high-level nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) jointly optimizes the subsystem state trajectories, arm torques, ground reaction forces (GRFs), and interaction wrenches, enabling online wrench design and optimization while preserving the dynamic coupling among the independently modeled subsystems. The optimized arm torques are applied directly for cooperative dual-arm manipulation, whereas the prescribed GRFs are mapped to lower-body joint torque for whole-body coordination. We validate the proposed framework through numerical simulations and hardware experiments on a G1 humanoid robot. The results demonstrate optimal interaction wrenches consistent with simulated contact measurement, cooperative dual-arm trajectory tracking, and stable whole-body coordination while executing the NMPC in online manner.

papers.title_en: HITCH: Teaching a Vision-Language Model to Operate a Humanoid through a Whole-Body Harness
papers.authors: Qingzhou Lu, Chenxin Liu, Xinming Wang, Liu Cao, Yanjiang Guo, Mengdi Xu, Jianyu Chen
papers.evidence: 视觉语言模型通过感知到全身运动的执行框架操控人形机器人
papers.tldr: 人形机器人由视觉语言模型控制时，既需要可靠的全身接口，也需要能跨任务迁移的身体操作知识。HITCH让感知返回VLM在图像中选定点的三维位置，并用学习跟踪器把骨盆、躯干、手、行走与视线命令转成全身运动。研究发现准确测量场景与执行命令都能提升任务成功率；再用教师策略经HITCH完成五个基础任务的轨迹微调VLM。无任务专属轨迹时，模型在SIMPLE和HumanoidArena成功率分别为51%和42.5%，每个SIMPLE任务增加五条轨迹后SIMPLE升至95%；真机G1无真实训练数据也能搬箱并走向目标。
papers.abstract_en: Enabling vision-language models (VLMs) to control humanoid robots requires both reliable whole-body interfaces and knowledge of how to use the body that carries over across tasks. We present HITCH (Harness Interfaces To Command Humanoids), a harness in which perception returns the 3D position of any point the VLM selects in its image, and execution turns commands for the pelvis, torso, hands, walking, and gaze into whole-body motion with a learned tracker. We find that both measuring the scene and executing commands accurately raise task success. We then fine-tune a VLM on trajectories in which teacher policies solve five base tasks through HITCH, so that it learns how to operate the humanoid. Without task-specific trajectories, the fine-tuned model completes 51% of SIMPLE episodes and 42.5% of HumanoidArena episodes, and adding five trajectories per SIMPLE task raises its SIMPLE success to 95%. On a real G1, it carries a box and walks to a goal without real training data.

papers.title_en: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
papers.authors: Vongani H. Maluleke, James Ni, Kie Horiuchi, Lea Wilken, Jiahui Lei, Evonne Ng, Roei Herzig, Jitendra Malik, Trevor Darrell, Angjoo Kanazawa
papers.evidence: 面向人形机器人的分层全身运动生成与跟踪控制
papers.tldr: 现有人形机器人多作为孤立智能体训练，难以与人类伙伴进行自然身体协调。Social Humanoid 提出分层系统，基于伙伴动作在29自由度Unitree G1上生成并执行社交响应式全身运动。高层策略用共享token化表示建模人-人形运动序列，可生成反应动作并在遮挡时预测伙伴；底层控制器负责跟踪执行。作者构建260小时HHI基准，并在仿真与真实世界验证协调、类人行为。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid robots are typically trained as solitary agents, leaving them unable to coordinate physically with human partners who naturally anticipate and adjust to one another. To bridge this gap, we present Social Humanoid, a hierarchical system that generates and executes socially responsive whole-body motion on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 conditioned on a human partner's motion. Its high-level policy performs flexible sequence modeling of human and humanoid motion through a shared tokenized representation, generating reactive humanoid motion and anticipating the partner's motion when they are occluded, while a low-level whole-body tracking controller executes the generated motion on the robot. To train the system, we introduce a two-phase adaptive retargeting procedure that retargets one interaction partner to the robot while morphing the other partner to preserve contact dynamics, reachability, and relative body scale. We apply this procedure across five motion-capture datasets to produce a new Human-Humanoid Interaction (HHI) benchmark of 260 hours of human-humanoid interactions. Our results demonstrate that Social Humanoid produces coordinated, human-aligned behavior across diverse interaction types in simulation and the real world. Project page: https://von31.github.io/social-humanoid/

papers.title_en: ForPC: Force-Aware Whole-Body Control for Precise Humanoid Cart Pushing
papers.authors: ZhenYu Zou, Xing Liu, ShiChuang Wang, YunLong Dong, LiNan Deng, Feng Hua, Jun Wan, Cheng Cheng
papers.evidence: 面向人形推车的力感知全身控制
papers.tldr: 人形机器人推轮式小车可搬运重物，但双手抓握形成力耦合闭环，接触力驱动小车的同时扰动平衡，负载变化也改变耦合动力学。ForPC 采用两阶段强化学习：先学习负载与姿态变化下的行走先验，再以机载观测推断力与状态潜变量，残差策略协调手臂、腰腿和基座速度。仿真中相较仅行走基线，速度 RMSE 最多降 68.2%，多弯道路径横向 RMSE 最多降 74.2%；零真机训练迁移至 Unitree G1，无负载专项调整可推 30 kg 小车达 0.5 m/s。该工作展示人形机器人无需改造场地即可高效搬运的潜力。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid robots are expected to take over strenuous material handling in manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare, where operating existing wheeled carts would let them move heavy loads without modifying the workplace. However, humanoid cart pushing remains challenging because the bimanual grasp closes a force-coupled loop in which the contact wrenches that drive the cart also disturb the robot's balance, and payload changes alter the coupled dynamics. We propose ForPC, a force-aware whole-body control framework that regulates cart velocity through two-stage reinforcement learning. A locomotion prior is first trained under varied hand loads and upper-body postures to provide balance support. A force latent and a state latent are then inferred from onboard observations, without external force sensors, and fed to a residual policy that coordinates bounded arm, waist, and leg adjustments with base-velocity commands. Multi-objective rewards penalize bimanual internal opposition, grasp slip, and actuator saturation, encouraging the policy to apply contact force on demand without human demonstrations. Sim-to-sim experiments show that ForPC reduces cart-velocity RMSE by up to 68.2% relative to a locomotion-only baseline (Loco-only) and cross-track RMSE by up to 74.2% on the multi-bend route. Trained solely in simulation, the policy also transfers to a physical Unitree G1 without real-world training or fine-tuning and, with no payload-specific adjustment, pushes a cart carrying up to 30 kg at 0.5 m/s. These results suggest that humanoid robots could eventually replace humans for efficient material handling in daily life.

papers.title_en: SUGARv2: Learning Diverse Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Skills from Synthesized Interaction References
papers.authors: Tianshu Wu, Tianxiang Gui, Yue Chen, Tingxu Liu, Ziye Peng, Guangjie Yang, Xiangqi Kong, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang, Hao Dong
papers.evidence: 通过合成交互参考学习多样视觉人形移动操作技能
papers.tldr: 视觉人形机器人全身移动操作技能扩展时，示教采集与任务专属训练设计成本高。SUGARv2 把可复用任务模板适配到不同空间布局，合成协调的机器人与物体运动参考，并以参考模仿作为跨任务统一学习目标。先训练特权教师，再经教师蒸馏与强化学习得到视觉策略，配合多样物体实例与视觉域随机化。五个任务仿真平均成功率 91.0%，真机部署完成 sim-to-real 迁移。
papers.abstract_en: Scaling up visual humanoid loco-manipulation skill acquisition requires reducing the human effort needed as tasks and spatial configurations expand, particularly in demonstration collection and task-specific training design. We present SUGARv2, a unified framework for learning diverse visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills through interaction reference synthesis and a shared training pipeline. To obtain diverse references at low cost, we adapt reusable task templates to different spatial configurations, synthesizing coordinated robot and object motions. To reduce task-specific reward design and training effort, we use reference-based imitation as a common learning objective across tasks. We first train privileged teachers to execute these references, then train visual policies through teacher distillation and reinforcement learning with the same reference-based mimic rewards, using diverse object instances and visual domain randomization to support visual generalization and sim-to-real transfer. Across five humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, SUGARv2 achieves a mean success rate of 91.0% in simulation. Deployment on a real humanoid robot further demonstrates successful sim-to-real transfer for whole-body manipulation. These results demonstrate the framework's potential for learning diverse visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills.

papers.title_en: DKWBC: Decoupling Motion Tracking and Balancing for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
papers.authors: Dingkun Wei, Zehong Shen, Huaijin Pi, Xueyang Wang, Xing Zhu, Hujun Bao, Yujun Shen, Xiaowei Zhou
papers.evidence: 解耦运动跟踪与平衡的人形全身控制
papers.tldr: 人形全身控制需同时跟踪多样动作并维持平衡，现有强化学习跟踪器将二者耦合学习，面对相似姿态的不同动态需求时易学习困难并产生高频抖动。DKWBC将基于模型的逆动力学前馈与关节PD反馈用于跟踪力矩，再由残差策略学习平衡力矩修正。仿真和真机表明，单一平衡策略可跨动作数据集泛化，在地面支撑、附加负载和物理交互下保持跟踪与平衡。该解耦结构降低了学习难度，为人形动态控制提供了可扩展方案。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid whole-body control requires a robot to track diverse reference motions while maintaining balance under gravity, torque limits, contact switching, and external disturbances. Existing reinforcement-learning-based trackers typically learn control outputs that jointly address motion tracking and balance. However, similar reference poses can correspond to substantially different dynamic demands, requiring a unified policy to learn motion-dependent control requirements alongside balance corrections. This can complicate learning and lead to high-frequency fluctuations in control outputs. We propose DKWBC, a dynamics-informed whole-body control framework that combines explicit model-based tracking with a learned balancing residual. Inspired by the model-based and environmental-wrench contributions to joint torques in floating-base dynamics, DKWBC uses inverse-dynamics feedforward and joint PD feedback to supply tracking torques, while a residual policy learns additional joint-torque corrections for balanced execution. By explicitly accounting for motion-dependent torque demands, this structure simplifies the policy's learning task. Experiments in simulation and on real hardware demonstrate that a single learned balancing policy generalizes across motion datasets while maintaining accurate motion tracking and balance across ground support, attached payloads, and physical interaction. Project page: https://robbyant-research.github.io/DKWBC/.

papers.title_en: DreamVLA: From Generated Human Motions to Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.authors: Kevin Park, Izat Rasyad, Dvij Kalaria, Shankar Sastry
papers.evidence: 用生成人体运动引导仿真强化学习训练人形VLA策略
papers.tldr: 人形VLA训练依赖昂贵遥操作数据，仿真RL又受任务奖励设计制约。DreamVLA用生成人类运动轨迹引导仿真RL，产出可靠执行轨迹，并以参考条件DAgger蒸馏纠正离线模仿的分布偏移。方法在平台抓取、开抽屉、按按钮及行走抓取任务上评估，并消融DAgger轮次、残差RL与生成数据规模。其意义在于无需新任务遥操作数据即可在仿真中训练人形VLA策略。
papers.abstract_en: Training vision-language-action (VLA) policies typically depends on substantial robot demonstration data, making human teleoperation a costly and cumbersome bottleneck, particularly for whole-body humanoid interaction. Reinforcement learning in simulation offers an alternative for scaling this data, but designing task-specific rewards remains challenging. To address this, we propose DreamVLA, which uses generated motion trajectories to guide reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation, converting them into reliable task execution trajectories. These trajectories train VLA models in simulation without new task-specific teleoperation data. Our central contribution is a reference-conditioned DAgger distillation procedure: after a failed learner rollout, we restart the RL expert from a sampled learner state with the same reference suffix and aggregate successful corrective trajectories, addressing the distribution shift left by offline imitation. We evaluate picking from a platform, opening a drawer, pressing a button, and walking and picking from a platform, with ablations of DAgger iterations, residual RL, and generated dataset scale. Project website: ember-center-berkeley.github.io/DreamVLA.

papers.title_en: Kimodo-Policy: Learning Kinematic Action Models for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Yunheng Wang, Jiaxi Zhang, Wei Lu, Yuetong Fang, Taowen Wang, Yixiao Feng, Shuning Zhang, Junzhe Xu, Yichi Wang, Zizhao Yuan, Kailun Huang, Lusong Li, Mingqian Zhou, Zecui Zeng, Renjing Xu
papers.evidence: 基于运动学动作模型与VLA先验的人形机器人移动操作
papers.tldr: 人形机器人全身移动操作需要高维动作的持续协调，而视觉语言动作模型等先验未必刻画机器人运动本身的结构。作者提出运动学动作模型KAM，把全身运动作为直接预训练目标，并以预训练运动生成器作为动作生成主干。首个实例Kimodo-Policy将冻结的Kimodo文本到运动主干与轻量ControlNet视觉条件结合，用根-躯干-手分层协调移动与操作，并借运动历史与重复动作块预测衔接运动合成与闭环控制。在HumanoidArena多任务上取得72.14%最高总成功率，真实八任务平均60%。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires continuous coordination of high-dimensional whole-body motion to realize task objectives. While vision-language-action models and world action models transfer semantic and visual-dynamics priors to robot control, these priors do not necessarily capture the structure of robot motion. We introduce Kinematic Action Models (KAMs), a paradigm that treats whole-body motion as a direct pretraining target and uses a pretrained motion generator as the primary action-generation backbone. KAMs ground learned temporal and cross-body coordination priors through task conditioning, visual observations, and execution feedback. We present Kimodo-Policy as an initial instantiation, combining a frozen Kimodo text-to-motion backbone with lightweight ControlNet-based visual conditioning. A root-body-hand hierarchy coordinates locomotion and manipulation, while motion-history conditioning and repeated action-chunk prediction bridge motion synthesis and closed-loop control. Following large-scale loco-manipulation pretraining, the policy achieves the highest overall success among compared policies on multi-task HumanoidArena (72.14%), competitive performance on SIMPLE, and 60% mean success across eight real-world tasks, with 678M parameters (92M trainable). Ablations support the contribution of the pretrained motion backbone. Together, these results provide initial evidence for motion generation as a complementary foundation for humanoid action learning.

papers.title_en: HINT-VLM: Humanoid Interactive Navigation over Rough Terrain with Embodiment-Grounded Vision-Language Model
papers.authors: Ziwon Yoon, Seok Hwan Kim, Yiyu Chen, Quan Nguyen, Lu Gan, Ye Zhao
papers.evidence: 基于视觉语言模型的崎岖地形人形交互式导航与规划
papers.tldr: 人形机器人在崎岖地形导航时，需同时判断地形可通行性与物体可移动性，但传统方法与NAMO多假设平坦环境且交互反应式。HINT-VLM提出混合规划框架，用VLM语义先验结合高斯过程残差模型，以本体交互数据校正可移动性估计。该方法将概率可移动性纳入分层不确定性感知规划，联合利用行走与操作。作者称这是首个面向崎岖地形NAMO的预测式可移动性推理方案。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid robots have achieved significant progress in locomotion and manipulation, enabling traversal over rough terrain and richer interaction with the environment, such as moving obstacles. However, most traditional navigation methods assume non-interactive environments and focus only on traversal. While Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO) approaches relax this assumption, prior efforts have largely focused on flat environments and reactive interaction, rather than predicting object movability and planning ahead. These limitations become critical in outdoor rough-terrain scenarios, where robots must jointly reason about terrain traversability and object movability. In this work, we address NAMO for humanoid robots in cluttered outdoor rough terrain by proposing a hybrid planning framework that combines semantic priors from a Vision-Language Model (VLM) with embodied robot interaction data through a Gaussian process (GP) residual model. The GP corrects the VLM-derived movability prior to produce embodiment-grounded probabilistic movability estimates, which are then incorporated into hierarchical uncertainty-aware planning. The proposed approach allows humanoids to jointly leverage locomotion and manipulation for efficient and safe navigation, representing the first solution to NAMO in rough terrain through predictive movability reasoning and probabilistic VLM integration.

papers.title_en: Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids (DASH): Latency-Agnostic Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models for Humanoid Manipulation
papers.authors: Bingzhang Wang, Nathan Zhao, Jialeng Ni, Jiayin Zheng, Yin Zhang, Kehua Chen, Jian Yao
papers.evidence: 面向人形灵巧操作的异步解耦VLA模型
papers.tldr: VLA闭环控制中，视觉语言骨干处于控制关键路径，动作执行时观测已陈旧，骨干越大反应性越差。DASH将慢速VLM与快速flow-matching动作头解耦为LCM并发进程，控制频率仅由动作头决定；动作头融合冻结骨干的陈旧语义与自身ResNet的新鲜视觉，并以异步训练和自适应时序聚合应对部署时延。异步RoboTwin上，0.8B至8B骨干均保持20Hz，同步基线从9.7降至4.1Hz，且DASH各规模成功率更高；真实人形灵巧手抓放也优于同步流程。该工作实现延迟无关的VLA扩展。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models pair a vision-language backbone with an action head, but in closed-loop control the backbone sits on the control-critical path: while it computes, the robot keeps moving, so each executed action is conditioned on an increasingly stale observation. A larger backbone therefore directly blocks reactivity, especially in humanoid dexterous manipulation. We present DASH, a Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids that removes this coupling. DASH splits the policy into a slow vision-language model (System 2) and a fast flow-matching action head (System 1) that run as concurrent processes over the LCM communication protocol, so the control rate is set by the action head alone, independent of backbone size. The action head fuses stale semantics from a frozen backbone with fresh vision from its own ResNet encoder, desynchronized training exposes it to the staleness it meets at deployment, and an adaptive temporal aggregator aligns overlapping action chunks under variable inference latency. On an asynchronous RoboTwin benchmark that charges inference latency in simulated time, DASH holds 20 Hz control rate from 0.8B to 8B backbones while the synchronous rate falls from 9.7 to 4.1 Hz, with higher success at every size. On a real humanoid with dexterous hands, DASH achieves clearly higher pick-and-place success than the synchronous pipeline.

papers.title_en: LHNav: Long-Horizon Humanoid Navigation via Multirate Coordination and Physics-Grounded Action Data
papers.authors: Xueyang Wang, Zehong Shen, Dingkun Wei, Huaijin Pi, Changpeng Wang, Xing Zhu, Hujun Bao, Yujun Shen, Xiaowei Zhou
papers.evidence: 结合全身运动的长时程人形导航
papers.tldr: 长程语言指令下的人形多目标导航需在连续全身运动中保持任务进度，现有任务分解或路点方法难以兼顾。LHNav 将导航组织为不同时间尺度的 Brain、Cerebellum、Brainstem 三角色，并以进度与到达反馈异步协调任务推理、VLA 运动 token 预测和全身控制。其物理数据引擎生成沿避障路线、跟踪更准确的示范并配对视觉观测。仿真中单目标成功率与运动平滑性优于 OmniNav 和 DualVLN，长程任务成功率达75.56%，并在 Unitree G1 上实现真实环境零样本长程执行。
papers.abstract_en: We study humanoid navigation across multiple destinations under long-horizon language instructions. This task is challenging because robots must maintain progress across successive goals while continuously producing natural, stable whole-body motion through confined spaces. However, task decomposition in existing methods does not by itself ensure progress throughout execution, while waypoint-based navigation does not guarantee natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. Our key idea is to organize navigation into three complementary roles operating at different time scales: a Brain for task reasoning, a Cerebellum for local motion generation, and a Brainstem for whole-body execution. We realize this idea in LHNav, an asynchronous system that uses progress and arrival feedback to coordinate navigation goals, VLA motion-token prediction, and whole-body control. To train the Cerebellum for natural, route-faithful motion, we develop a physics-grounded data engine that improves physical tracking of motion references along collision-aware routes and pairs the resulting demonstrations with rendered visual observations. Together, these designs allow task planning to proceed alongside continuous movement and extend single-goal navigation to successive destinations with natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. In simulation, our navigation VLA outperforms OmniNav and DualVLN in single-goal success and motion smoothness, with fewer collisions and falls. Using a VLA trained only on single-goal demonstrations, LHNav achieves a 75.56% success rate on long-horizon navigation tasks. Deployment on the Unitree G1 further demonstrates single-goal navigation and zero-shot long-horizon task execution in real-world environments, including layouts with repositioned objects. Project website: https://robbyant-research.github.io/LHNav/.

papers.title_en: RedirectMimic: Local Motion Content Redaction for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
papers.authors: Zepeng Wang, Xiaochuan Shi
papers.evidence: 基于编辑参考跟踪的人形全身控制
papers.tldr: 人形机器人运动接口需在保留参考行为的同时支持局部动作替换，但仅移除跟踪激励会导致替代动作不受约束。RedirectMimic 将 actor 观测到的参考与训练执行所用的目标分离，用规则生成的编辑参考在 PPO 中引导跟踪奖励，部署接口保持不变。在 Unitree G1 上，过顶手臂任务的核心窗口内容出现率降至 2.7%，核心窗口关节成功率 94.2%，替换误差最低。该方法实现了内容抑制、无跌倒执行与局部保留的兼顾，为局部运动内容红action提供了有效方案。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid motion interfaces should accommodate application-specific movement constraints while retaining useful reference behavior. Local content redaction requires a controller to replace selected movements even when it continues to receive the original reference. Removing the tracking incentive for those movements leaves their replacement unspecified. We introduce RedirectMimic, which separates the reference observed by the actor from the target used to train its execution. A rule-generated edited reference guides tracking rewards during proximal policy optimization, while the deployed observation and action interfaces remain unchanged. We evaluate pose- and speed-defined arm editing in Unitree G1 simulation using a tracker pretrained on 7,509 motion clips. On the overhead-arm task, RedirectMimic reduces core-window content occurrence to 2.7%, compared with 58.9% for reward zeroing and 32.8% for anti-tracking. It achieves 94.2% core-window joint success, combining content suppression, fall-free execution, and local retention. On the speed-defined task, fast outward arm movements occurred at similarly low rates under all three local editing methods. Across both tasks, RedirectMimic achieved the lowest replacement error among these methods and tracked unedited motions with accuracy comparable to that of the pretrained controller. Project page: https://xiaopeng-whu.github.io/RedirectMimic/.

papers.title_en: PERA: Plug-in Experts for Robotic Actions in Continual Whole-Body Control
papers.authors: Shangchao Hu, Yadan Sun, Xibo Yu, Wei Huang
papers.evidence: 仿真中即插即用专家的持续全身控制
papers.tldr: 人形机器人可通过动作模仿获得行走、舞蹈等全身技能，但全策略微调新技能会破坏已有行为，逐技能单独训练又会推高训练与维护成本。PERA冻结预训练混合专家策略，仅新增任务专家及其路由分数，并利用任务奖励或教师动作监督学习新技能。在Unitree G1仿真中，每个新增模块约占基础actor参数1.03%，十个新任务全部完成；禁用专家后126个原动作仍可完整执行。该工作实现可插拔的全身控制技能扩展，并显示专家收益可迁移到未参与训练的舞蹈动作。
papers.abstract_en: Motion imitation enables humanoid robots to acquire whole-body skills such as walking and dancing. However, fine-tuning an entire policy for a new skill can affect existing behaviors, while training a separate policy for each skill increases training and maintenance costs. We present PERA, a method for learning new skills by reusing existing motion capabilities. PERA freezes a pretrained mixture-of-experts policy and trains an additional task expert and its routing score using task rewards or teacher-action supervision. In Unitree G1 simulation, each added task module contains approximately 1.03% of the parameters of the base actor. Built on our pretrained policy, PERA successfully completes all ten new tasks. Disabling the expert restores the original computation path of the base policy, which still fully executes all 126 original motions. Enabling the expert also improves the execution of some dance motions not used to train that expert, indicating that its benefits extend beyond its training motions. Experiments with HoloMotion further demonstrate the applicability of PERA to different base policies.

papers.title_en: FORGE: Force-Aware Multi-Granularity Control for Efficient Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Liangjun Xing, Ke Fan, Kailin Li, Bin Wang, Xiaojie Niu, Qingwei Ben, Jiafei Cao, Wei Yao, Yebin Liu, Jingbo Wang, Weinan Zhang
papers.evidence: 涵盖速度导航与全身人形移动操作的力感知多粒度控制器
papers.tldr: 人形机器人移动操作需在频繁接触下协调行走、平衡与操作，遥操作演示采集困难。FORGE提出力感知多粒度控制，将命令空间从速度导航、足端落点细化到腕部位姿与可选力条件，训练无需全身轨迹或关节参考。系统用动量观测器与仿真接触力监督的残差修正估计腕等效力，无需腕部力传感器，并以准静态虚拟目标环自适应腕目标。实验验证统一控制稳定性、任务空间跟踪、持续接触挤压力估计及变负载蹲举扩散策略执行，为高效人形移动操作提供可部署方案。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated locomotion, balance regulation, and manipulation under frequent contacts, making teleoperated demonstration collection difficult: a practical controller must simultaneously provide precision, stability, and contact awareness. We propose FORGE, a force-aware multi-granularity control system with a coarse-to-fine command space spanning velocity navigation, planar foot placement, wrist-pose tracking, and optional force-conditioning inputs. Policy training requires no full-body human motion trajectories or joint-angle references; deployment consumes only sparse bilateral wrist poses relative to the pelvis, coarse motion commands, and optional desired wrist-load inputs. For sustained contact, FORGE combines a momentum observer with a learned correction trained using simulator contact-force supervision. At deployment, it estimates low-frequency, wrist-equivalent interaction forces from proprioception and reconstructed low-level arm PD torques, without wrist force/torque sensors. A quasi-static virtual-target loop uses this estimate and an optional desired applied-force input to adapt the wrist target. A frozen locomotion prior and asymmetric residual actions stabilize manipulation-induced whole-body corrections. Experiments evaluate unified-control stability, task-space tracking, quasi-static wrist-equivalent force estimation, squeezing forces during sustained contact with a rigid box, and downstream diffusion-policy execution of a squat-and-lift task across payload conditions. Website: https://bb0928.github.io/forge/.

papers.title_en: X-Nav Technical Report: Real-World Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor Navigation on a Humanoid Robot
papers.authors: Jiaxin Huang, Chengxing Lin, Xiaoyu Luo, Sirui Chen, Jingyu Guo, Aolin Li, Kairui Chen, Rui Zhen, Cheng Wen, Kerui Gu, Shunyao Wang, Zhihui Peng, Shaoli Huang
papers.evidence: 双足人形机器人的长时程室内外导航
papers.tldr: 双足人形机器人在单条语言指令下完成室内到室外的长程导航仍是难题，且步态会导致相机持续晃动。X-Nav构建从数据到部署的完整系统：数据引擎融合开源场景、数字孪生与真机数据，MELIOR仅用机载RGB图像预测动作或导航目标，X-Navarch将简短指令拆成子任务并执行目标导航与避障。在灵犀X2上，系统完成约百米办公楼大堂到邻楼商店的任务，可改目的地、穿门、上路并绕开动静障碍；数字孪生适配提升闭环成功率，MELIOR在R2R-CE/RxR-CE上也有竞争力。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon navigation from indoors to outdoors remains an open problem for humanoid robots: one instruction covers rooms, doors and roads, and the camera moves with the gait. Worken, AGIBOT's measure of productive robot work, depends on robots that reach their workplaces autonomously. We present X-Nav, to our knowledge the first system to take a bipedal humanoid through a language-instructed long-horizon mission from indoors to outdoors. X-Nav covers a pipeline from data to deployment. Its data engine collects navigation data in open-source scenes, in digital twins of deployment sites and on real robots. Its navigation model, MELIOR, takes only RGB images from the robot's built-in camera and comes in two versions: MELIOR-A predicts actions, and MELIOR-N predicts a navigation goal. Its agentic workflow, X-Navarch, turns a brief human instruction into sub-tasks and deploys MELIOR on the robot with explicit target navigation and obstacle avoidance. On the Lingxi X2, X-Nav completes a mission of about a hundred metres from an office lobby to a store in a neighbouring building; LiDAR and odometry are used for target approach and low-level control. The mission is completed with both versions of MELIOR: the robot follows a change of destination and walks through a door from the lobby to the road, and with X-Navarch it also passes static and dynamic obstacles on the route. During deployment, MELIOR is adapted with data collected in a digital twin of the site; the adaptation raises its closed-loop success rate in the twin, and the adapted model is then deployed on the robot at the real site. In addition, MELIOR achieves competitive results on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks.

papers.title_en: MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams
papers.authors: Yimin Han, Jiahui Zhang, Wanyue Li, Zeren Luo, Yeke Chen, Liu Zhao, Peizhuo Li, Xiaoyu Ji, Shihao Dong, Xuechao Chen, Zhangguo Yu, Annan Tang, Peng Lu
papers.evidence: 基于单目视频的感知驱动人形全身实时控制
papers.tldr: 单目视频实时驱动人形机器人全身控制面临运动重建与高频控制难以兼顾的问题。MoViC将单目人体运动重建、机器人重定向与基于Transformer的行为基础模型结合，并用频域运动表示提供时序上下文、减少输入维度。部署时通过外推方法衔接10Hz视觉估计与50Hz控制器，实现异步执行。硬件实验验证了高动态动作跟踪，以及仅凭实时单目RGB完成无穿戴双臂/单臂操作遥操作。
papers.abstract_en: Real-time whole-body imitation from monocular video requires both a robust universal tracker and high-quality real-time reconstruction. We present MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices. The framework combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model. The policy receives proprioceptive history, a single explicit next-step reference, and a compact frequency-domain motion representation that supplies temporal context without explicitly stacking future reference frames, which reduces the input dimension and network size. During deployment, our extrapolation method bridges the 10-Hz visual estimation with 50-Hz controller, enabling asynchronous visual processing and policy execution. Hardware experiments further demonstrate highly dynamic motion tracking and device-free teleoperation of bimanual and single-arm manipulation tasks from live monocular RGB input. Project page: https://movicproject.github.io/ .

papers.title_en: Driving the Style: Velocity-Conditioned Whole-Body Control from Motion Demonstrations
papers.authors: Murad Dawood, Oezge Drama Berkenkamp, Antonio Gonzales Marin, Nutan Chen
papers.evidence: 基于运动演示的速度条件人形全身控制策略
papers.tldr: 人形机器人模仿动捕演示时，对抗模仿难以迁移到硬件，全身跟踪策略又依赖运行时参考轨迹。本文用全身跟踪奖励直接训练策略，但仅让actor接收紧凑速度指令和机器人观测，参考运动只监督奖励与特权critic，无需教师蒸馏。在Unitree G1上，策略按速度指令复现全身风格，仿真成功率不低于98%且真机全部试验完成；在留出慢走速度剖面上，基线成功率显著下降。该工作无需运行时参考轨迹，兼顾部署可靠性与风格泛化。
papers.abstract_en: Achieving human-like behavior on humanoid robots has advanced rapidly by leveraging motion-capture demonstrations rather than hand-crafted cost functions. Adversarial imitation supplies a style signal that lets a policy fulfill a task while adhering to a desired style, but is difficult to transfer to hardware. Whole-body tracking through reinforcement learning instead deploys reliably and imitates demonstrations faithfully, but the resulting policies are conditioned on the future reference, so they require a reference trajectory at runtime and can fail when the motion differs from the training data. We train a humanoid policy directly with whole-body tracking rewards while restricting its actor to compact locomotion commands and robot observations. Reference motion supervises the reward and privileged critic, without supplying reference joint trajectories to the actor or requiring teacher distillation. The demonstrated style is thereby encoded in the policy through the tracking reward, so the robot reproduces the whole-body style under commanded velocities. Trained on a single random-walk motion and commanded with velocity profiles from held-out motions, our policy reaches at least 98\% success in simulation and completes every trial on the Unitree G1. On held-out slow walking, whole-body tracking drops to 2\% success and command-conditioned distillation to 56\%, and both fail on the real robot. On the trained motions, the joint position error of our policy stays within 8\% of whole-body tracking, and it has a higher style coverage than adversarial motion priors (AMP), which fell on the real robot without a safety crane.

papers.title_en: SemPhys: Semantic-Physical Co-Learning for Humanoid Motion Generation via Differentiable World Models
papers.authors: Zejian Kang, Yeqiang Wang, Zekai Chen, Boyang Shen, Mingyu Ma, Bingqian Wu, Fan Zhou, Jianjie Zhang, Chentao Shen, Wentao Yang, Rui Qian, Xiangru Huang
papers.evidence: 基于可微世界模型的语言驱动人形运动生成
papers.tldr: 自然语言驱动人形机器人全身运动时，参考轨迹经跟踪控制器执行后可能偏离原意，因此语义对齐应直接评估实际执行动作。SemPhys 用可微世界模型和固定跟踪控制器预测执行片段，将其插回完整轨迹并对指令打分，通过预测片段反向传播训练生成器，同时用配对锚定损失稳定适应。在 BONES-SEED 上，它基本保持参考到执行的指令检索精度，并在执行动作上取得最高检索精度，说明语义-物理协同学习能提升可执行动作的语义一致性。
papers.abstract_en: In human-robot collaboration, natural language lets people direct a humanoid's whole-body movements without programming joint trajectories. A common approach generates a kinematic reference from an instruction and relies on a tracking controller to execute it. However, as the controller maintains balance under contact constraints, the executed motion can depart from the reference in ways that change the action it conveys. Our central insight is that semantic alignment must be evaluated directly on the complete motion the robot physically executes. Building on this insight, we introduce \textbf{SemPhys}, a framework that trains motion generators using semantic feedback from simulated executions. A differentiable world model and a fixed tracking controller predict a short segment of a recorded execution. SemPhys inserts this prediction at its original position, scores the complete trajectory against the instruction, and backpropagates through the predicted segment. A paired anchoring loss stabilizes adaptation by keeping each generated reference close to its counterpart from the initial generator. On BONES-SEED, SemPhys largely preserves instruction retrieval accuracy from reference to execution and achieves the highest retrieval accuracy on executed motions among the evaluated methods.

papers.title_en: WEVO: World Model-Enabled VLA Optimization for Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Qianzhong Chen, Muyuan Lin, Yuyin Sun, Mac Schwager, Cheng-Hao Kuo, Roberto Martín-Martín
papers.evidence: 在世界模型中后训练全身人形VLA
papers.tldr: 人形机器人VLA后训练面临真实探索不安全、仿真RL受sim-to-real残差限制的问题。WEVO提出无需遥操作的框架，在动作条件视频世界模型中后训练全身VLA：用仿真play数据增强预测，并用每任务20次真实rollout校准世界模型，再与全身控制器组成闭环RL环境。三个真实任务中，视频世界模型RL将平均成功率由23.3%升至75.0%，优于真实机器人RL的48.3%。该工作结合仿真覆盖与部署对齐世界模型，为全身移动操作提供安全可扩展的后训练路径。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve vision-language-action (VLA) policies beyond imitation, but humanoid exploration is unsafe and simulator RL can exploit residual sim-to-real gaps. We present WEVO, a teleoperation-free framework for post-training a whole-body humanoid VLA in an action-conditioned video world model (WM). Simulated manipulation and locomotion play data improve contact-dynamics and viewpoint-change prediction. A VLA trained on synthetic demonstrations collects 20 autonomous real robot rollouts per task to align the WM with deployment observations. The VLA, whole-body controller (WBC), and video WM then form a closed-loop RL environment with dense progress rewards. Across three real robot tasks, play data improves every evaluated WM metric and downstream policy success; video WM RL raises mean success from 23.3% to 75.0%, compared with 48.3% for real robot RL. We therefore leverage the complementary strengths of both environments: simulation provides policy initialization and broad coverage, while the video WM offers a deployment-aligned environment for policy improvement. Project website: https://qianzhong-chen.github.io/wevo.github.io/.

papers.title_en: ECHO: In-Context Behavior foundation model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
papers.authors: Xingyi Wang, Bin Li, Jiyuan Shi, Chenyun Zhang, Weiji Xie, Xiangyu Miao, Junsong Wu, Wei Song, Shiqiang Zhu, Chenjia Bai
papers.evidence: 面向人形全身控制的情境内行为基础模型
papers.tldr: 人形行为基础模型能借大规模动作模仿与并行强化学习获得多样技能，但难以在变化物理条件下精确执行，易退化为保守折中。ECHO 将交互经验转化为环境特定控制，分离通用行为先验与动力学特定执行：以混合退火采样建立行为先验，再用上下文表示与残差适配从交互历史学习动力学表示，对冻结先验做残差修正，无需测试时更新参数。实验显示其在多种动作与物理条件下优于所有基线，并在 Unitree G1 上实现极端杂技、地形交互与负载自适应。该工作提供了可部署的上下文适应人形全身控制范式。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) acquire diverse skills through large-scale motion imitation and massively parallel reinforcement learning, yet broad behavioral capability does not ensure precise execution across physical conditions. Without distinguishing the underlying dynamics, policies may favor conservative compromises over environment-specific precision. We introduce ECHO, an in-context BFM that turns interaction experience into environment-specific control, separating general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution. Mixed and Annealed Sampling first establishes a behavior prior in a single pretraining stage by balancing targeted practice with broad motion coverage. Building on this prior, Context Representation and Residual Adaptation learns structured dynamics representations from interaction histories to guide residual corrections to the frozen prior, enabling adaptation without test-time parameter updates. Extensive experiments show that ECHO outperforms all baseline methods across diverse motions and physical conditions. Moreover, deployment on the Unitree G1 demonstrates whole-body teleoperation spanning extreme acrobatics and terrain interaction, alongside payload adaptation in manipulation and whole-body control. Page is available at https://mwondering.github.io/echo-bfm/

papers.title_en: $ζ_0$: A Framework for World Action Models with Joint Scene and Body Foresight in Humanoid Control
papers.authors: Yizhi Chen, Zhanxiang Cao, Yitong Wang, Junyu Liu, Hongchu Zeng, Xinyi Peng, Chuxuan Huang, Yicheng Su, Zihao Zhou, Shengcheng Fu, Haoyang Li, Liyun Yan, Tianyue Zhan, Jianming Ma, Yang Zhang, Keqi Zhu, Xiaxi Si, Jinming Yao, Qiao Sun, Shizeng Zhang, Jiangwei Zhong, Yue Gao
papers.evidence: 同时预见视觉与身体运动的人形控制世界动作模型
papers.tldr: 人形机器人交互需同时预判视觉与本体响应，仅视觉预判或潜空间损失难以直接监督动作反馈。ζ0将视觉-语言-动作策略转为世界动作模型，在共享潜表示中联合预判未来视觉特征和实测关节轨迹，并用教师参考响应与双响应迁移训练因果预测器，部署仅用因果预测。七个HumanoidArena任务上，基于Ψ0和GR00T N1.7达63.6%和79.5%成功率，较基座提升18.8和9.0点；六个真实任务达78.3%和85.0%。
papers.abstract_en: World Action Models anticipate visual outcomes to guide robot actions, yet humanoid interaction also depends on how the robot's body responds. Visual foresight alone can miss body motion, while latent-distance losses do not directly supervise action responses. We present $ζ_0$, a framework that turns vision-language-action policies into World Action Models by foreseeing future visual features and measured joint trajectories in a shared latent representation. During training, a teacher conditioned on recorded futures provides a reference action response, and dual-response transfer trains the causal predictor to match it through the teacher and the executing policy. All components are trained jointly, and deployment uses only causally predicted futures. On seven HumanoidArena tasks, $ζ_0$ built on $Ψ_0$ and GR00T N1.7 reaches 63.6% and 79.5% mean success, 18.8 and 9.0 points above these bases. On six real-world tasks, it reaches 78.3% and 85.0%, gains of 16.7 and 10.0 points. On GR00T, its 79.5% tops all compared seven-task joint policies. Project page: https://chenyizhi123.github.io/zeta0-project/

papers.title_en: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
papers.authors: Yue Huang, Tianshan Zhang, Zeyu Zhang, Jayeon Kang, Akide Liu, Sungjoon Choi, Dacheng Tao, Hao Tang
papers.evidence: 基于Mamba扩散的长时程可控人形运动生成
papers.tldr: 长时程、实时可控的人体动作生成对交互动画与人形机器人至关重要，但现有自回归扩散方法受限于有界注意力缓存与重复去噪开销。Motion Mamba 2.0 提出基于 Mamba 的根—身体扩散架构，融合局部注意力、可恢复循环状态与持久内容记忆 PCM。在 HiPHI 上实现最长 39.52 秒的精确终点控制，RTX 4090 上中位延迟从 1685.35 ms 降至 276.14 ms，配对加速 6.138 倍。并在 Unitree G1 上验证了文本引导动作组合与交互式控制。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overhead. We present Motion Mamba 2.0, a Mamba-based root-body diffusion architecture that integrates local attention, resumable recurrent states, and persistent content memory (PCM) for long-horizon controllable motion generation. PCM transforms compressed motion history from Mamba recurrent states, together with state changes and text-conditioned features, into dynamically updated content slots accessible to local attention. To enable efficient inference, we further develop an execution scheme tailored to this architecture, combining CUDA Graph replay, fused kernels, and execution-flow simplification while preserving the canonical history update. Evaluations on retargeted HiPHI demonstrate accurate terminal control over rollouts of up to 39.52 s, while short-horizon comparisons on BONES Seed and retargeted HumanML3D show that the model also retains strong spatial control and text-motion matching. On an RTX 4090, the optimized execution reduces median complete-window latency from 1685.35 to 276.14 ms, achieving a median paired speedup of 6.138$\times$ while preserving identical outputs and committed states in the tested rollouts. Moreover, we conduct extensive real-world evaluation on the Unitree G1, demonstrating sequential text-guided action composition, expressive motion, and interactive locomotion through keyboard and mouse control.

papers.title_en: CHAMP: Coordinated Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Whole-Body Motion Priors
papers.authors: Lijun Han, Muyuan Ma, Zichen Wang, Siyuan Liu, Yuxi Liu, Yutong Wang, Bohao Zhang, Heng Zhou, Wei Sui
papers.evidence: 面向协调人形移动操作的全身运动先验
papers.tldr: 人形机器人全身移动与灵巧操作协调控制仍难，关键是如何从异构数据学习可迁移的全身运动先验。CHAMP先用约2298小时人机数据预训练视觉语言模型，预测未来身体与手部运动，并以共享表示统一不同具身数据。随后用面向协调的动作专家CAE结合稀疏路由融合多层特征，联合生成身体和手部动作。在Unitree G1上，七项仿真与七项真实任务成功率分别达84.8%和91.4%，长程爆米花服务任务达70.0%。
papers.abstract_en: Coordinating locomotion and dexterous manipulation is fundamental to humanoid robots operating in human environments. A key challenge is learning motion priors from diverse data and using them effectively for coordinated robot control. We present CHAMP, a unified framework for humanoid loco-manipulation that combines whole-body motion pretraining with adaptive feature extraction. CHAMP pretrains a vision-language model to predict future body and hand motion from approximately 2,298 hours of heterogeneous human and robot data. A shared motion representation enables unified whole-body motion learning across embodiments from datasets with body annotations, hand annotations, or both. To ground these motion priors in robot control, we introduce a Coordination-oriented Action Expert (CAE) and train it on replay data generated using the target controller. Through sparse routing, CAE adaptively selects, transforms, and fuses features from multiple layers of the pretrained model to jointly generate body and hand actions. In experiments, CHAMP achieves overall success rates of 84.8% on seven simulated tasks and 91.4% on seven real-world tasks with a Unitree G1, outperforming the evaluated baselines in both settings. In particular, CHAMP achieves 70.0% success on the long-horizon popcorn-serving task, compared with 40.0% for the best-performing baseline.

papers.title_en: Zero-HLM: Generalizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation without Real Robot Data
papers.authors: Dianyi Yang, Mengya Liu, Zhumei Wang, Yu Liu, Xiaochen Zhang, Yixuan Li, Le Ma, Yuhang Yang, Weiqi Huang, Wei Liang, Baoxiong Jia, Siyuan Huang
papers.evidence: 真实到仿真再到真实的人形训练数据与物理仿真
papers.tldr: 真实机器人数据成本高昂，限制了人形机器人全身移动操作的可泛化学习。Zero-HLM提出从真实到仿真再回真实的框架，用手机拍摄结合高斯引导的智能体重建，并通过动作与环境的协同自适应生成可执行全身参考。它构建了4800条物理验证演示，在Unitree G1的三项任务上实现零样本迁移。仿真训练的GR00T N1.7平均全任务成功率达66.7%，优于真实数据训练的46.7%；在泛化配置下，仅扩大仿真训练就把汇总成功率从23%提升到69%。
papers.abstract_en: Learning generalizable humanoid loco-manipulation remains bottlenecked by costly real-world demonstrations. Simulation provides a scalable alternative, but requires visually faithful, physics-ready scenes and executable whole-body motions. We present Zero-HLM, a real-to-sim-to-real framework that transforms smartphone captures and simulated source demonstrations into scalable training data for humanoid loco-manipulation. Gaussian-guided agentic real-to-sim reconstruction aligns visual and physical scenes; motion-environment co-adaptation uses rollout feedback to correct whole-body references and interaction geometry. We generate 4,800 physically validated demonstrations for zero-shot transfer across three Unitree G1 tasks. Simulation-trained GR00T N1.7 achieves 66.7% mean full-task success, versus 46.7% with real-data training. On generalized configurations, expanded simulation training raises pooled success from 23% for base-trained real-data policies to 69%, without additional real demonstrations. Project page: https://young-bit.github.io/zero-hlm/

papers.title_en: Learning Multi-Phase Robot Loco-Manipulation via Phase-Conditioned Policy Optimization
